clue.text: Class progress endlessly at university

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to cut the final letter off the word meaning progress

parts.note: to progress is to grow
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student class is advancing without pause through university.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a set or category, the same sense as a class in a classification.

clue.text: Common soldiers in Britain have nickname for one of their own

indicators.note: in tells us the soldiers sit inside the abbreviation for Britain

parts.note: GB is the standard abbreviation for Great Britain
OR, other ranks, are the common soldiers below officer level

parts.words: nickname for one of their own
parts.note: LIMEY is a slang nickname, chiefly American, for a Briton

explanation.surface: British rank-and-file troops have a pet name for a fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common soldiers' looks like one phrase, but 'Common' is the definition: gorblimey as an adjective means vulgar or lowbrow, from the Cockney oath.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective this Cockney oath describes things vulgar or lowbrow, the 'common' of a snob's put-down.

clue.text: Crone forged old note

indicators.note: forged suggests something faked or made up, so the letters of crone are reshaped

explanation.surface: An old woman has faked a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: This was slang for a one-pound note, a banknote long withdrawn in Britain.

clue.text: Vulgar large building one leaves to be with Scottish fellow

indicators.note: leaves means the word for one departs from the building word

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a stately home to live with a Scotsman, which is thought crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plebeian is common or coarse, belonging to the lower orders, so vulgar in the old sense.

clue.text: Liverpudlian with obsession about caning

indicators.note: about places the word for obsession around the Liverpudlian word

parts.note: a thing, as in 'he has a thing about trains', is an obsession
WACK is a Scouse term of address, so it stands for someone from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A man from Liverpool fixated on corporal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: WACK (or wacker) is Liverpool slang for a pal or fellow Liverpudlian; Liverpool is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Caning someone means beating them with a stick, which is giving them a hard blow or smack.

clue.text: Several players start to tackle England's former captain

indicators.note: start to takes just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Rio Ferdinand once captained the England football team

explanation.surface: A football report about a former England skipper making the first tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians, and three performers count as several players.

clue.text: The two of us stepping out in part of Yorkshire, once

parts.note: two people speaking of themselves say we
striding means walking out with long steps

explanation.surface: A couple taking a brisk walk across the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large county in northern England, was divided into Ridings until 1974; this was one of the three.
explanation.definitionFit: This was one of the three historic administrative divisions of the county, abolished in 1974.

clue.text: Little boy overcome by bully, dropping in field

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcome by puts the boy's name beneath the bully word

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or bully them
Pat is the short form of the boy's name Patrick

explanation.surface: A small lad is beaten by a bully and falls over in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb about the boy falling, but it is the noun: a piece of dung.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat of cow dung is the sort of excrement found lying in pasture.

clue.text: Hotel owner takes quick look around during meal if starter's off

indicators.note: during places the reversed look inside the meal word
starter's off means the meal word loses its first letter

parts.note: dinner is a main meal

indicators.note: around turns the quick look word backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A hotelier peers around at dinner when the first course has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the look backwards and 'if starter's off' beheads the meal; 'during' sets one inside the other. 'Starter' looks like a first course but is a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs a hostelry, which is a small hotel or pub with rooms.

clue.text: Service in high performance car is hard work

indicators.note: in places the service inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring car
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Maintaining a sports car is a tough job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a car service, but it is an armed service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is British informal for strenuous labour, as in 'years of hard graft'.

clue.text: Cor! Skier hurtles round back of these alpine homes

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters wrap around the final letter of these
hurtles suggests wild motion, so the letters of cor and skier are thrown about
back of takes the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a skier careers around behind some mountain chalets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurtles' rearranges CORSKIER to ROCKERIS, and 'round' puts it around E, the back of 'these'. The homes are for alpine plants, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock gardens are where alpine plants are grown, so they are homes for alpines.

clue.text: Working during week with a chocolatier

indicators.note: during places the working word inside the abbreviation for week

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Working through the week alongside a chocolate maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Wonka is the fictional sweet-maker of Roald Dahl's children's novel, a famous maker of chocolate.

clue.text: You want colourful birds? Crows no good

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: to glory is to exult or crow, so glories means crows

explanation.surface: Someone after bright plumage is told crows will not do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like the birds, but it is the verb: boasts or exults.
explanation.definitionFit: Lories are small brightly plumaged parrots from Australasia.

clue.text: Carriageway in Al wider than all the others

indicators.note: in places the carriageway word inside the word for first-rate

parts.note: A1, printed here as Al, means first-class or best
a carriageway is a road

explanation.surface: A stretch of road on Britain's A1 is the widest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads A1 as the British trunk road, but A1 is first-rate, BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of broad means the most wide, exceeding every rival in width.

clue.text: Properly cured, say, being able to afford private medicine?

definitions.text: being able to afford private medicine?

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the phrase is spoken

parts.note: well healed means properly cured

explanation.surface: Being nicely recovered, and having the money to go private.
explanation.walkthrough: Well-heeled means wealthy, which is what private medical treatment requires; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthy, the idiom for being rich, lets someone pay for private healthcare.

clue.text: Naughty madam's keen to put things right

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of madam's keen are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written with its s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly behaved woman wants to set things straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to compensate for a wrong, the idiom for setting matters straight.

clue.text: Writers' Bible?

parts.note: Stephen King is a novelist
Henry James is a novelist

explanation.surface: A holy book written by authors?
explanation.walkthrough: Two writers, Stephen King and Henry James, together name the famous English translation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Authorised Version of the scriptures, published in 1611, is known by this monarch's name.

clue.text: Colleague in top post

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the phrase top post

explanation.surface: A coworker holds a senior position.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a partner or opposite number at work.

clue.text: Weapons one carried as a rule

indicators.note: carried means the weapons word holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: ordnance is military weaponry, especially artillery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: As a rule, a single gun was carried.
explanation.walkthrough: The near-twins ORDNANCE and ORDINANCE differ only by the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, such as a local by-law.

clue.text: Olympic venue once accommodating a legendary female runner

indicators.note: accommodating means the venue holds the letter a inside it

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics

explanation.surface: A past Olympic city housed a fabled sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this huntress outran her suitors and lost only to Hippomenes and his golden apples.

clue.text: Wrench for a New Yorker?

explanation.surface: A spanner suited to someone from New York?
explanation.definitionFit: To pull sharply is to wrench, and an American, especially a northerner, is called this informally.

clue.text: In all, rude and tetchy, principally? Possibly so

definitions.text: In all, rude and tetchy, principally? Possibly so

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement
principally takes the first letter of tetchy

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone, overall, is crude and irritable at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges IN ALL RUDE plus T, the first letter of 'tetchy'; the whole clue describes a bad-tempered person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surly and rude, irritable in temper, is bad-tempered by nature.

clue.text: Initially terrible score: out for a duck

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
initially takes the first letter of terrible

explanation.surface: A dreadful cricket score: a batsman out for nought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing; here 'a duck' is the definition, a sea duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Hurried to stop sailor being captured at sea?

indicators.note: to stop means the hurried word plugs the sailor word, holding it inside

parts.note: hied is an old word for hurried
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor was rushed off, having been taken prisoner at sea?
explanation.definitionFit: A ship seized by force is commandeered, as pirates seize vessels at sea.

clue.text: During dispute he's flipping angry

indicators.note: flipping turns the extracted run of letters back to front
during means the letters sit within the words dispute he's

explanation.surface: In an argument, a man is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' takes PUTEH from 'dispute he's', and 'flipping' reverses it; flipping also reads as a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and agitated is the informal idiom for being upset or cross.

clue.text: Container of fluid reduced suffering

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz

indicators.note: reduced means the suffering word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: agony is great suffering

explanation.surface: A bottle of medicine eases pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or cider, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Habits associated with old actress

parts.note: habits are clothes, and garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Nuns' clothing linked to a veteran star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' looks like customs, but it is clothes (as in a nun's habit). Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was the Swedish film star famous for wanting to be alone.

clue.text: Fish for tea daily

explanation.surface: Fish for one's afternoon brew each day.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is three things: a trout-like fish, British slang for tea, and a cleaning woman, also called a daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish is a cold-water trout relative, the drink is slang via Chinese cha, and the cleaner is a charwoman.

clue.text: Try putting worker on short time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An attempt to put an employee on reduced hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To try someone in the old sense is to test or entice them, as in 'lead us not into temptation'.

clue.text: Record with most of Wagner cycle includes female in title role

indicators.note: includes means the record word holds the female word inside it

parts.note: a log is a written record
a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the cycle word

parts.note: Wagner's Ring cycle is his set of four operas

explanation.surface: A recording of much of Wagner's operas featuring a woman as the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Lohengrin is the title character of Wagner's opera, though not part of the Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin, the swan knight, is the hero who gives his name to Wagner's 1850 opera.

clue.text: Rejected pornographic material penned by model man of letters?

indicators.note: penned by means the model word encloses the turned-back material

parts.note: a poser is someone who poses, as a model does

indicators.note: rejected means the word for smut is sent back, so read backwards

parts.note: dirt is smutty or obscene material

explanation.surface: A model has written out some discarded smut, like a writer of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the smut backwards and 'penned by' sets it inside the model. 'Man of letters' looks like a writer, but is a mounted carrier of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postrider carried mail on horseback, a courier of correspondence.

clue.text: 14 early in the afternoon

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, and an afternoon hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 refers to 14-across, MAKE AMENDS. Read as two words, the answer is one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make reparation for a wrong; split in two it gives one o'clock, just after noon.
